title: fix(runtime): the package install and enable routes announce metadata:reloaded
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DMscMg6AKHasj3ZXEDorLPH)_

Fixes #33302

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no authorable key, value or metadata type moves; the change is which runtime doors announce an existing kernel event

Opened by `domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cykhsWAtSL6Sr4VWFG` (area A5 of the server area-lease pilot), from claim comment 6884323409.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：运行时的 `POST /packages` 安装与 `PATCH /packages/:id/enable` 启用两条路由，在包进入服务后向内核宣告 `metadata:reloaded`（载荷 `changed: ['app/ID']`，与市场本地安装同一拼法）。安装每次落地都宣告；启用只在包原本处于停用时宣告。
- 为什么改：这两条路由原来什么都不宣告，所有 `metadata:reloaded` 订阅者（岗位改名 `renamedFrom` 的任职人迁移、流程重同步、钩子/动作/翻译重同步）都听不到，要等下次重启。
- 风险与回滚：多一次已有的内核重同步（与发布、本地安装同一事件，订阅者幂等）；宣告失败只记 `warn`，不改变路由的应答。回滚即回退本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` 中新增的 `announcePackageReload` 与启用路由里的 `wasDisabled` 判定；`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-reload-announce.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/packages-reload-announce.test.ts`，预期 5 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`
  - New module helper `announcePackageReload(deps, context, id, door)`, used only by the two handlers below. It calls `deps.announceKernelEvent(context, 'metadata:reloaded', { changed: ['app/ID'] })`, the spelling the marketplace install-local door uses (`announceHotInstall` in `@objectstack/cloud-connection`). A subscriber failure is caught and logged once at `warn` with the restart that repairs it, the level the publish-drafts door and install-local use for the same announce. It never changes the door's answer.
  - `POST /packages`: announces after the registry write and the durable state write, on both answers. That includes the `enableOnInstall` lifecycle refusal, which refuses the switch but not the install, whose row is already served.
  - `PATCH /packages/:id/enable`: reads `registry.isPackageDisabled(id)` before `enablePackage` (the predicate `enablePackage` itself asks before it tells its enable listeners). It announces only when the package was disabled, so an enable of an already-enabled package announces nothing.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-reload-announce.test.ts`: new pin file (5 cases).
- `.changeset/33302-package-doors-announce-reload.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` patch.

The A2 hunk in this file (open PR #33276, around line 2997, a different handler) is not touched.

## Why

After the hot-install carry landed, `plugin-security` carries the holders of a renamed position (`renamedFrom`) on `metadata:reloaded`. Neither of these two doors announced that event, so a package they brought into service kept its renamed positions' holders on the old names until the next boot. The same went for every other subscriber of the event.

Premise re-measured on `origin/main` (9499dcc530) through the real route before the fix: the same pin file with `packages.ts` at that commit answers `4 failed | 1 passed`, and the holder assertions read `{ e1: 'sales_rep', ... }` and `{ i1: 'field_rep' }`: the holders stayed on the old names.

One part of the card's premise is narrower than written. `ManifestSchema` declares no `positions` key, so a `POST /packages` body can never carry a position. A probe of `ManifestSchema.safeParse` with `positions` answers `unrecognized_keys: ["positions"]`. An authored package's positions are registered by a publish, and that publish already announces `position/NAME`. The install door puts a renamed position into service in one way only: an overwrite install with `enableOnInstall: true` of a disabled package. The install-side holder pin therefore drives that path. A fresh install is pinned on the announcement itself.

## Tests

`packages-reload-announce.test.ts` uses a real `ObjectKernel` with the SQL driver (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`), `ObjectQLPlugin`, the real `SecurityPlugin`, and an `HttpDispatcher` over that kernel. The holder move is `plugin-security`'s own carry. A recorder hook only listens, and reads whether the registry holds the named package when the event arrives.

1. Enable door: a code package renaming `sales_rep` is disabled, then enabled through `PATCH /packages/:id/enable`. The holder moves to `crm_sales_rep`, the control holder is untouched, and exactly one announcement `{ changed: ['app/ID'] }` arrives with the package registered.
2. Enable of an already-enabled package: answers 200 and announces nothing.
3. Fresh install through `POST /packages`: one announcement, with the package registered.
4. Overwrite install with `enableOnInstall: true` of a disabled authored package whose published position renames `field_rep`: the holder moves to `authored_sales_rep`, with one announcement.
5. A subscriber that throws: the install still answers 201, the package is registered, and the failure is said once at `warn`, naming the package.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts` (module doc, "When it runs") still lists "the runtime's package install and enable routes" as doors that register positions without announcing. That sentence is now false. The file is outside this card's surface, so it is reported for the seat and not edited here.
- The disable door and `DELETE /packages/:id` still announce nothing. The install-local uninstall does announce the withdrawal. Whether these two should was left out of scope by the card, and the report covers it.

## Verification

Local verification after this head (typecheck, the runtime suite, the derived gate families and the `--ran` reconciliation) is in the `os-dev-report` comment on #33302. CI check-runs are the authority for every family CI runs.
